profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at a university audio ML lab for a proposal to revisit Masked Conditional Neural Networks (MCLNN) on ESC-10 as part of a reproducibility-and-extension workshop submission. The proposal keeps the original MCLNN core idea but updates the training stack, adds light audio augmentation, and plans a compact ablation study plus qualitative inspection of learned frequency-band masks. The agenda is to judge whether the current experiment design is mature enough to receive shared GPU time, whether the proposed ablations are sufficient for the review packet, and what needs to be documented before implementation freeze. The expected outcome is a conditional approval of the design with a short list of modifications and documentation items.

members.name: Dr. Mira Voss
members.expertise: Environmental sound recognition, experimental methodology, benchmarking in low-resource audio tasks
members.background: Mira leads a small academic lab that has previously reproduced several classic audio architectures and maintains an internal benchmark repository for ESC datasets.
members.private_state: She wants this proposal approved quickly so the team can secure workshop visibility without overcommitting scarce compute; she is mainly trying to ensure the design is methodologically defensible and comparable to older lab results.
hidden_assumptions: When researchers say the 'front-end' is unchanged in an audio model, they usually mean the acoustic feature extraction settings such as spectrogram type, mel bins, and window/hop parameters, not the masked layer geometry inside the network.

A proper ablation for a model-centric paper should isolate architectural ingredients of MCLNN itself, while training conveniences like augmentation and crop policy can stay fixed unless they are a claimed contribution.
The lab's cleaned ESC-10 cache used in recent internal benchmarks is effectively the canonical ESC-10 setup for comparison purposes, even if it differs slightly from untouched upstream files.

For an internal design review, a study is 'reproducible enough' once there is one documented end-to-end run per fold and the mean result lands close to the historical target, because exact publication-grade robustness comes later.

members.name: Jonah Lee
members.expertise: PyTorch experimentation, reproducibility tooling, audio preprocessing pipelines
members.background: Jonah joined the lab from an industry speech team and has been refactoring older research code into containerized, tracked experiment pipelines.
members.private_state: He wants the proposal to lock in stronger engineering standards so he does not have to revisit the study later; he is also trying to avoid another loosely specified benchmark that becomes hard to audit.
hidden_assumptions: In MCLNN, the mask bandwidth and overlap are part of the model's effective front-end because they implement the filterbank-like inductive bias, so 'same front-end' implies keeping those settings fixed.

If the proposed recipe includes augmentation, crop policy, or optimizer conventions that could materially move accuracy, those belong inside the ablation matrix rather than being treated as invisible infrastructure.
The 'official ESC-10 folds' are the raw ESC-50 fold assignments filtered to the ten ESC-10 classes, unless someone explicitly says they are using a lab-cleaned derivative.
A result is not truly reproducible unless it includes repeated seeds, variance reporting, and artifact tracking for every comparison line that may appear in the review packet.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both agree to keep 'the same front-end' for fair comparison.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the acoustic feature extraction remains the same as prior MCLNN work: same log-mel representation, same frame size, same hop, and same input normalization; mask geometry can still be tuned as part of the model review.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means both the acoustic features and the MCLNN mask bandwidth/overlap settings remain fixed, because the mask is functionally part of the frequency-band front-end.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In audio ML, 'front-end' is used loosely for both preprocessing and early inductive-bias layers, so the phrase sounds fully aligned and neither person expects it to hide a boundary difference.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the 'ablation matrix'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both say the proposal should include a 'complete ablation matrix'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects ablations only over core MCLNN design elements such as masking, conditional context width, and order, with augmentation and crop policy held constant across rows.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the ablation matrix to cover any performance-relevant part of the end-to-end recipe, including augmentation, temporal crop policy, and other training-stack additions wrapped around MCLNN.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both treat 'complete ablation' as a standard phrase from good experimental practice, so they do not enumerate row-by-row content during the meeting and the scope gap stays implicit.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to running on the 'official ESC-10 folds'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the lab's legacy ESC-10 preprocessing repository, which uses the familiar five folds but omits a handful of files that were flagged during an old cleanup pass.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the untouched ESC-50 fold metadata filtered down to the ESC-10 classes, including all original files.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both setups are routinely described inside the lab as 'official ESC-10 folds,' the file-count difference is small, and mature public benchmarks create a false sense that the reference object cannot be ambiguous.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree the design should be 'ready for reproduction' before approval.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks readiness means one clean run per fold, documented commands, and average accuracy near the expected historical number so the design can be approved for compute.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks readiness means three seeds per fold, variance tables, and tracked checkpoints/artifacts for each comparison line before the design can really be considered reproducible.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both value reproducibility and use the same approval language, but internal reviews in the lab often leave the exact threshold unstated because everyone assumes they share the same standard.

turns.inner_thought: I want this to be a fast approval if the design is defensible. We do not have budget for a sprawling benchmark exercise. If Jonah can show the updated MCLNN setup lands near our historical ESC-10 numbers with one clean pass per fold, that's enough to justify shared GPUs and get the workshop plan moving.

If we're close, I'd like to leave with a short list of changes and a documentation freeze point rather than reopening the whole study.

I also want to signal that the package should actually be reproducible, not just executable once. If I can get that expectation in now, I won't have to retrofit the pipeline later.

The aim is to revisit the old result in a way that still feels faithful, but with cleaner tooling and enough structure that the extension pieces are easy to review.
